title: רב נחמן בר יצחק
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness
attribution: Fresh project English, authored from the frozen Hebrew and revised through source-informed author and independent model review. Editorial-layer attribution in the Warsaw witness remains qualified.

paragraphs:
(a) Rashi considers him unqualified Naḥman; Tosafot says that figure is bar Yaakov. Rashi says he was the nasi's son-in-law, hence needed no help from that household; Tosafot says because he was wealthy. See unqualified Naḥman above at length. Although his father was Mar Shemuel's scribe, he was not ordained. Bava Metzia 16b: Naḥman says his father was among Shemuel's judicial scribes. On Rashi's view, Yitzḥak was the scribe, as Yuḥasin writes here; on Tosafot's, Yaakov was, as Yuḥasin also writes. Thus he assigns one document to two people, although he himself favors Tosafot. Some support seemed to me Beitzah 25b: bar Yitzḥak says he brought Mar Shemuel from sun to shade; his father's scribal role would explain his familiarity.

There seemed some support for Rashi that unqualified Naḥman is bar Yaakov [the source's formulation conflicts with its opening and is retained]: Megillah 28b and Ein Yaakov, Mo'ed Katan, tell of a man who taught Sifra, Sifrei and Tosefta and died. They asked Naḥman to eulogize him. He asked how: a basket full of books that was lost? 'See the difference between the forceful of the Land of Israel and the pious of Babylonia.' Rashi calls this bar Yitzḥak, among Babylonia's pious, who told the reciter at Sotah's end not to teach that fear of sin had ceased, for he was present. Ein Yaakov specifies bar Yitzḥak; our Gemara leaves Naḥman unqualified. On Heilprin’s reading of Ein Yaakov, Megillah’s pious Naḥman is bar Yitzḥak, as Rashi says. In our Gemara both names are unqualified, so the identification remains open. Shabbat 37b calls bar Yitzḥak a master of deeds; Rashi: meticulous in conduct. This could support Rashi's identification of pious unqualified Naḥman with him. Yet שס״ח [provisionally the new Shas], variant readings, prefers books reading unqualified Naḥman there, so doubt remains.

(b) It says Naḥman son of Rav Ḥisda called him 'a maneh son of a half-maneh,' Seder Ta'aniyot; this is mistaken, see 21b. Bar Yitzḥak called himself that, and Ḥisda's son a maneh son of a maneh. He used half-maneh because his father Yitzḥak was not ordained with the title Rav. Shabbat 156b: astrologers told his mother he would be a thief. She never allowed his head uncovered, telling him to cover it for fear of Heaven and pray against the evil impulse. He did not know why. One day, studying beneath a palm, his covering fell; he saw the tree, his impulse prevailed, and he climbed and bit off a date cluster. Yoma 22b, I Samuel 13, 'Shaul was a year old when he reigned': Huna says like a year-old who had not tasted sin. Bar Yitzḥak objects: perhaps like a child soiled with mud and excrement? He saw a nightmare and said he submitted to the bones of Shaul ben Kish. Another nightmare followed; he said he submitted to Shaul ben Kish, king of Israel. He was sensitive, Yoma 30a. Yosef praised his exposition as Sinai; Maharshal deletes bar Yitzḥak—see unqualified Naḥman above.

Ketubbot 22: bar Yitzḥak discusses a deed issued before a court, perhaps an impudent court, etc., naming Ravna Ashi's court. Rashi says Ashi is named as academy head at Mata Meḥasya in bar Yitzḥak's days. Menaḥot 102a: Ashi says he stated the teaching before Naḥman. Tosafot reads Kahana, the later Kahana in Ashi's time, not Naḥman, Rava's teacher, who died before Rava; Ashi was born when Rava died. Reading bar Yitzḥak would work. End of quotation; they follow their distinction between the Naḥmans. This solution does not satisfy me. Yuḥasin, amoraim by generations, generation 5, citing Dorot Olam and R.Sh.G. [רש״ג; provisionally Rav Sherira Gaon], says bar Yitzḥak headed the academy for four years after Rava and died 4117—see part 1, 4113. Shenot Ḥayyim, Metzora 123c, says Rava died 663 of the era of deeds and bar Yitzḥak 666. Ashi, born at Rava's death, would be only three or four when bar Yitzḥak died. How could he state teachings before him, or be academy head in his lifetime as Rashi says? Very puzzling; requires examination. Yuḥasin, citing the epistle of R.Sh.G. [רש״ג; provisionally Rav Sherira Gaon], gives death 663, equivalent to 4115. He lived long; he appears in Ammi and Assi's days and Ashi's, which requires examination. He carried Sabbath utensils in and out, asking, “If R. Ammi and R. Assi visited me, would I not carry things for them?”; some say if Yoḥanan visited, Shabbat 119a. Whether he saw Yoḥanan, Ammi and Assi requires examination.

(c) Abba Mari the exilarch, his father-in-law. R. Avin in his time. Rav Adda bar Ahavah (see his entry). Rav Avya. Rav Aḥa the Galilean spoke to him. Rav Aḥa—another version, R. Ḥiyya bar Yosef—leaned on his nephew Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak's shoulder. R. Ammi and R. Assi in his generation (see above). Amemar in his name. He reported in R. Assi’s name, Ḥullin 5b—requires examination. Rav Ashi in his generation (see above). Rav Bivi bar Abaye spoke to him. Giddel of Naresh. Rav Huna son of R. Yehoshua, his colleague. Rav Huna bar Natan visited him. R. Ḥuna in his name. R. Ḥiyya bar Abba. R. Ḥiyya of Hormin in his name. He asked R. Ḥiyya bar Avin, Bava Batra 97a, and told him, 'May your mind rest, for you have set mine at rest,' Pesaḥim 32b; he spoke to him, Berakhot 6; Shabbat 100b. R. Ḥama, R. Yehoshua's father. He spoke to R. Ḥanan son of Rav Ḥisda. He reported in Rav Ḥisda’s name, Avodah Zarah 63a. In R. Yehoshua ben Levi's name. R. Yoḥanan bar Ravina in his time. R. Yosef Tzirna'ah in his time, according to Yuḥasin—I did not find his mention. R. Yaakov bar Idi. Mar bar Ravina asked him. Rav Naḥman son of Rav Ḥisda (see above). He told Rav Pappa in Rava's name, Keritot 8a; his colleague, צ״ד [source notation unresolved]. In Rav's name, beginning of Ein Omedin; He reported in Rav’s name, Sukkah 46a. Rava, his teacher, Tosafot Bava Batra 46b. Rava was angry with him, there 86a; see Lo Yaḥpor. Rabbah bar Shumna in his time. He reported in Rabbah bar Avuhah’s name, beginning of BaMeh Ishah. Ravina asked him. Rav Shalman taught before him. He served Mar Shemuel (see above). Whether some notices I wrote under Naḥman bar Yaakov belong here requires examination.
